messages:
maya: Quick Q re: trace-derived SLO for gen-api — should we split latency by routing_policy (fast-path vs batch) in the dashboard? Rollout UX might want per-policy SLOs.

tom: Yes. Fast-path p95 is ~30ms, batch p95 is ~350ms. If we lump them together small regressions in fast-path disappear. Also we lose the cost signal. :thinking_face:

sasha: Agree on separation, but this multiplies cardinality (route x model x policy x region). We need to decide retention/rollup strategy before we add tags everywhere.

alex: What about keeping routing.policy on spans, then precomputing hourly rollups (p50/p95/error_rate) into metrics DB? Keep raw traces only for 7d for most routes.

maya: We currently send OTLP -> otel-collector -> clickhouse. How heavy is adding routing.policy attribute on every span?

sasha: Attribute itself is cheap on write (a few bytes), expensive on query if you don't pre-aggregate. Proposal: precompute per-route+policy aggregates, store rollups for 1h/6h/24h windows, raw traces 7d, 30d for critical routes. That keeps queries cheap.

tom: Example collector config I tried for adding the attribute:```yaml
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: routing.policy
        action: insert
        value: ${ROUTING_POLICY}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes]
      exporters: [clickhouse]
```

And a sample ClickHouse query (pseudocode):```sql
SELECT
  routing_policy,
  quantile(0.95)(duration_ms) AS p95,
  countIf(status_code >= 500)/count() AS error_rate
FROM traces
WHERE service = 'gen-api' AND timestamp >= now()-1h
GROUP BY routing_policy
```

alex: Also add cached_prefix_hit=true/false to spans — that explains a lot of variance in fast-path.

sasha: Retention tradeoffs: raw traces 7d default, 30d for top 20 routes by traffic, 1y aggregated rollups. That gives us regression debugability without insane storage. Need cost estimate.

maya: UX note: console should default to the combined SLO (so teams don't get noise), but offer a toggle to split by routing_policy and cached_hit. Show a small impact chart that projects error-budget burn if you exclude batch. Tooltip explaining why split matters.

tom: Can we wire these derived SLOs into canary gating? e.g., block rollout if p95_fast_path increases >10% and error_rate_fast_path > 0.5% in last 30m.

devops-bot: ingest-config updated in staging: collectors now add routing.policy attribute. https://ci.internal/repo/1234 :shipit: 

ingrid: Heads up — per-policy SLOs will increase metrics exports and query counts. I'll coordinate with finance to update quota docs and warning banners in console.

maya: Thanks. I'll open an RFC with retention/rollup numbers + console mockups. Action items: tom -> publish clickhouse query templates, sasha -> cost + storage estimate, alex -> PR for collector attr and cached_hit tagging, ingrid -> quota docs update.
